title: Goodfire says its new ‘inside-out’ monitors catch rogue AI agents at a fraction of the cost
slides: Can Goodfire's inside-out monitors catch rogue AI at low cost?
Goodfire's new method looks inside AI models to spot deception.
But it only works for known rogue behaviors, not new ones.
If you're deploying AI, now you can afford continuous monitoring.
Test Goodfire's monitors yourself—don't wait for a breach.
thread_text:
1. Inside-Out Monitoring

Goodfire's new method peers inside AI models to spot deception—without heavy compute costs.

2. Known Threats Only

It catches rogue behaviors it's been trained on. New, unseen tricks slip through the cracks.

3. Affordable Continuous Watch

If you're deploying AI, you can now afford to monitor around the clock, not just spot-check.

4. Test Before Breach

Don't wait for a rogue AI incident. Run Goodfire's monitors on your own models and see what they catch.

5. Your Move

Take a model you use, enable the monitor, and try to trick it. What happens? That's your real risk picture.

carousel_slides.hook: Rogue AI hides where you can't see
carousel_slides.description: New inside-out monitors catch deception cheaply, but only for known rogue behaviors—unseen tricks still slip through undetected.
Its method spots deception by looking inside models, cutting compute costs so monitoring becomes affordable for more teams.
Trained on specific rogue behaviors, it misses new, unseen tricks—leaving a blind spot for novel AI deception.
If you deploy AI, lower costs let you watch around the clock instead of spot-checking—catching issues before they escalate.
